title: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open on Escape, and a default dialog must still close
status: Open and labelled confirmed. A maintainer-side fix is proposed in pull request #43077, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model; it is kept for comparison after it merges.
summary: keyboard: false only calls preventDefault() on the native cancel event. Escape does not count as user activation, so after a few presses Chromium fires cancel with cancelable=false and the dialog closes anyway.
dependencies: dist/css/bootstrap.min.css: the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 stylesheet from npm (MIT); the repository does not commit built CSS
consumer: Author-written payment confirmation page around the unchanged TypeScript source at pinnedCommit, served with types erased by Node's built-in stripping. The page turns off the dialog transition and moves focus on shown.bs.dialog, so that the separate initial-focus issue #43120 does not affect this task. A second, ordinary dialog with the default options is on the page for the added guard.
addedAfterReview: Added after reviewing the engine-v11 patch for bootstrap6-dialog-escape-keyboard-false: it passed every frozen check by cancelling every Escape keydown, so an ordinary dialog with the default keyboard: true no longer closed on Escape. The page now also has a default dialog, and a guard requires Escape to close it. Earlier patches are replayed against this stricter task without inference.
